decisions.reason: The product is a natural extension of the established portfolio, publicly mentioned on the website, and sunk development costs favor persistence.
Given the firm's visible commitment and investment in this product line, escalation of commitment makes withdrawal unlikely.
The product has been publicly launched and aligns with existing capabilities, so dropping it would write off investments and invite justification costs.
Because the firm has committed to the product on its website and incurred development costs, persistence is more likely than exit.
The product is close to the established range and has public visibility, reinforcing escalation of commitment to keep it.
Sunk costs and the public commitment on the website make management reluctant to drop the product within the coming year.
